title: Namibia's Energy Bets: Venus Oil, Shell's $400m Write-down, $10bn Hyphen | The Six, Ep. 28
lede: Nearly five years after TotalEnergies announced the Venus discovery off Namibia, the decision to develop it has still not been taken, as terms with the government remain under negotiation. Alongside oil, Namibia is betting on green hydrogen, where the flagship Hyphen project's first-phase decision has moved to the end of 2027.
keyPoints: Venus was found in February 2022, about 290 km offshore under roughly 3,000 m of water; the discovery well reached 6,296 m (Offshore Technology).

TotalEnergies now plans Venus at about 150,000 barrels a day, down from an earlier 160,000, with first oil around 2030; terms with the government are still being negotiated (African Energy Week; Bloomberg via World Oil).
Shell wrote down about $400 million on its PEL 39 block in January 2025 after nine wells, citing low permeability and a high gas-to-oil ratio (Maritime Executive; The Namibian).
In September 2026 TotalEnergies completed a swap with Galp to take 40% and operatorship of the Mopane licence, PEL 83, and targets a decision there in 2028 (Galp; World Oil).

Hyphen Hydrogen Energy, a project of more than $10 billion in which the government holds 24%, plans up to two million tonnes of green ammonia a year; its first-phase decision is now targeted for the end of 2027 (New Era; The Namibian).
